claims.value: Grant retrospectively estimates Beauregard’s May effective force as probably not much over 50,000, reports a Union-side estimate of it as 70,000, and gives the Union force as roughly 120,000.
claims.rationale: The memoir distinguishes a retrospective effective estimate from an attributed wartime estimate, without an exact estimation date. The Union population basis is unspecified. These are not interchangeable opening counts or calibrated ranges.

citations.locator: Chapter XXVI, local extraction row 547; paragraph begins: Beauregard, however, was reinforced by Van Dorn immediately after Shiloh with 17,000
citations.quote: With these reinforcements and the new regiments, Beauregard had, during the month of May, 1862, a large force on paper, but probably not much over 50,000 effective men. We estimated his strength at 70,000. Our own was, in round numbers, 120,000.

claims.rationale: No common operation-opening time, area or both-side population basis is established. Do not substitute May totals or an enemy estimate for reviewed opening strengths.

claims.value: Grant recalls Logan telling him, probably on May 28, that the enemy had been evacuating for days.
claims.rationale: A retrospective report of a conversation with explicitly uncertain timing. It does not establish delivery to Halleck or the complete information available to him.

citations.quote: Later, probably on the 28th of May, General Logan, whose command was then on the Mobile and Ohio railroad, said to me that the enemy had been evacuating for several days

claims.rationale: A contemporary order or message chain establishing Halleck’s receipt, timing and assessment of evacuation evidence was not inspected. Grant’s retrospective criticism is not an independent reconstruction of that information set.

claims.value: NPS describes Halleck’s armies advancing on Corinth as a vital rail center.
claims.rationale: The source identifies an operational target, not an inspected pre-operation directive, a utility weight or an independent success to add to battle residuals.

citations.quote: the Union armies under Maj. Gen. Henry Halleck advanced on the vital rail center of Corinth.

claims.value: Grant says Halleck assumed field command on April 11 and named him second in command; Grant nevertheless describes orders going directly to subordinate formations while bypassing him.
claims.rationale: Formal position and exercised authority are not identical. Grant is an interested retrospective narrator, and his account does not adjudicate command effectiveness or assign outcome credit to every listed general.

claims.value: NPS describes Beauregard evacuating Corinth for Tupelo on the evening of May 29–30; Grant describes Union occupation without opposition after the evacuation.
claims.rationale: Record withdrawal and occupation without turning Grant’s adjoining counterfactual criticism into a measured command effect.
